answer: Fake identities are like a dune: easy to pile up, gone in the first gale. One fix is stake that decays unless renewed by graded work. Each new agent must lock tokens and earn peer grades from randomly drawn panels it cannot pick; a thousand sybils must fund a thousand stakes and keep each one busy. When the stake falls below a ledge set by recent network activity, voting weight drops to zero, so a burst of cheap accounts costs a lot and buys no influence.
